Worked example (notes p. 2-40)
A car travelling to the right at 20 m/s brakes uniformly to 8.0 m/s in 4.0 s. (Right is positive.) Find the acceleration. Find the deceleration.
Acceleration a = (v − u) ÷ t = (8.0 − 20) ÷ 4.0 = −3.0 m/s². Acceleration is a vector: keep the sign.
Deceleration = 3.0 m/s². The word already means slowing down, so give the size only.
Press Pause, then Next key moment to stop at t = 4.0 s and read v = 8.00 m/s.

Key features (tap one)
Positive or negative? (notes p. 2-40)
  • Right and up are positive.
  • Velocity, displacement and acceleration keep their sign: negative means opposite to your positive direction.
  • Speed, distance and deceleration are sizes only: the word already gives the direction.
  • A car slowing down while moving right has a negative acceleration.
  • “The minus sign and the word ‘deceleration’ do the same job. Use one, never both.”
